steps.message:
I looked at the repo before touching anything. This is a destructive change, so I want a yes before I write it.

**What the drop actually does:** `migrations/003` would run `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` against production, where the README says `users` has 48,000 rows. Every value in `notes` is deleted at that moment. The migrations here have no `down` files, so there is no rollback path in-repo — recovery would mean restoring from a database backup.

Two things I can't confirm from the code, and the request's wording doesn't settle them:

- "We stopped using it" — I can only see this repo. Nothing here reads `notes`, but nothing here reads any column; there's no application code in the tree. Any other service, report, or query against this database is invisible to me.
- Whether the 48,000 rows' `notes` values are backed up or exported anywhere before they go.

Also worth knowing: `schema.sql` is kept in sync by hand, so it needs the same edit, and SQLite only supports `DROP COLUMN` from 3.35 (2021) onward — older engines need the table-rebuild dance.

steps.message:
Done.

- **`migrations/003_drop_notes.sql`** (new) — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the comment style of 001/002.
- **`schema.sql`** — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the hand-maintained mirror matches post-migration state.

Nothing else changed; no commit made. Two things I did not do and you may want to handle before the deploy job runs this:

- **No backup step.** You confirmed the drop, so this is the plain version — the `notes` values for those 48,000 rows are gone the moment it applies. If a pre-migration dump isn't already part of the deploy, that's the only recovery path.
- **SQLite version.** `DROP COLUMN` needs 3.35+. I couldn't verify the production engine version from this repo; on anything older this migration errors out rather than silently misbehaving, so it'd fail loudly at deploy.

I ran no tests — the repo has no test setup or migration runner to exercise.
